product.amstrad-pc5086.summary: The XT option in the Series 5 retained the 8086 and 8-bit cards in a compact VGA desktop.
product.amstrad-pc5086.history: Documented in Amstrad's 1991 manual, the PC5086 was the 8086 option in the Series 5, alongside the 286-based PC5286. The range targeted professional work in limited desk space and offered Counterpoint for accessing DOS with a mouse. The PC5086 retained the XT architecture and was offered with one or two floppy drives, or a 40 MB hard disk.
product.amstrad-pc5086.warning: Research entry. Firmware is preserved and an inherited model exists in the code, but this entry does not certify validated startup or offer a creation profile.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.market: It was the XT alternative in a compact professional range. The combined 1991 manual documents PC5086 and PC5286; the Series 5 brochure explains its professional positioning and Counterpoint.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.commerc: Storage varied with the package purchased. The manual specifies one or two 720 KB floppy drives and a 40 MB hard disk option; the PC5286's 1.44 MB drive is not attributed to the PC5086.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.cpu: It could slow down for older software. The manual documents an 8 MHz 8086, switchable to 4.77 MHz through SPEED, and a socket for an optional 8087-2.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.memory: Main memory followed the conventional limit of XT PCs. The manual specifies 640 KB at 00000h–9FFFFh; EMS memory required an expansion card.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.video: VGA broadened the graphics capabilities of this XT architecture. The manual states MDA, CGA, Hercules, EGA, MCGA and VGA compatibility; it reserves C0000h–C7FFFh for the video BIOS.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.storage: The drives supported floppy or hard disk operation. The manual documents 3.5-inch 720 KB drives, a 40 MB hard disk and a disk BIOS at C8000h–C9FFFh; the exact drive model remains pending.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.interfa: Peripheral connections and two expansion cards were supported. The manual specifies DE-9 serial, DB-25 Centronics parallel and two half-length 8-bit ISA slots.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.firmwar: Two files attributed to the PC5086 are preserved. The 86Box collection supplies sys_rom.bin, 64 KiB, and c800.bin, 8 KiB; hashes were checked, but physical provenance and revision remain unknown.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.verifie: This revision establishes documentation and preservation, not operation. The manual, hashes and presence of the pc5086 model in BluMach code were checked; no firmware was executed.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.limitat: The entry remains under research until the machine is validated. Video ROM and physical revisions need identification, startup and peripherals need testing, and a creation profile needs preparation; the preserved files do not prove a complete set.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.manual: The original manual distinguishes the configurations of both models. PC5086/PC5286 User Manual, PC Guide 1-3, 4-3, 7-2, 8-4 and 8-6/8-7.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.brochur: The brochure places the machine within its range. The new Amstrad Series 5, August 1991: professional positioning and Counterpoint; PC5286-specific specifications are not transferred to the PC5086.
product.amstrad-pc5086.technical.firmwar: The collection makes the preserved files traceable. 86Box ROMs, machines/pc5086 directory, revision c4cd8da9034a8557896ff6a975ae58499a83bb80; it does not establish who read the chips.
